sentenceSets.sentence: His deftness at handling difficult questions made him an effective spokesperson during the most challenging period of the crisis.

answerChoices.reasoning: Skill means the ability to do something well, very close to deftness, but skill is broader and does not necessarily convey the smooth facility that deftness implies.
Adroitness means skillfulness and cleverness, nearly synonymous with deftness, but adroitness emphasizes cleverness in addition to facility.
Facility means ease and fluency in doing something, very close to deftness, but facility can be passive ease, while deftness implies active skill.
Competence means the ability to do something adequately, close to deftness, but competence emphasizes adequacy, while deftness implies smooth skill and ease.
Expertise means specialized skill or knowledge, related to deftness but emphasizing depth of knowledge rather than smooth facility.
Proficiency means a high degree of skill or competence, related to deftness but emphasizing mastery rather than smooth ease.
Aptitude means natural ability or talent, related to deftness but emphasizing innate ability rather than demonstrated skill and facility.
Finesse means delicate and sophisticated skill, related to deftness but emphasizing elegance and subtlety rather than overall facility.
Clumsiness means lack of grace or skill, opposite to deftness; the spokesman handled questions skillfully, not clumsily.
Ineptitude means lack of skill or ability, opposite to deftness; his effective handling of questions shows skill, not ineptitude.
Awkwardness means lack of grace or comfort, opposite to deftness; the spokesman's ease in handling questions contradicts awkwardness.

sentenceSets.sentence: The basketball player's deftness at ball handling allowed her to evade defenders through narrow gaps and create opportunities for her teammates.

answerChoices.reasoning: Skill means ability in doing something, very close to deftness, but skill is more general and does not necessarily convey the smooth facility and ease.
Agility means ability to move quickly and easily, close to deftness in physical performance, but agility emphasizes quickness rather than technical skill.
Finesse means skillful and delicate handling, very close to deftness, but finesse emphasizes elegance and subtlety rather than overall facility.
Coordination means harmonious working of body parts or people, close to ball handling but not describing the skill and ease that deftness conveys.
Talent means natural ability or gift, related to deftness but describing innate ability rather than demonstrated facility and skill.
Technique means a way of carrying out a procedure, related to ball handling but describing the method rather than the skill and ease.
Precision means exactness and accuracy, related to skilled ball handling but not describing the facility and ease of movement.
Control means the ability to manage or direct something, related to ball handling but not specifically describing the smooth facility that deftness conveys.
Clumsiness means lack of grace or skill, opposite to deftness; the player evades defenders skillfully through narrow gaps, not clumsily.
Awkwardness means lack of grace or ease, opposite to deftness; the smooth ball handling contradicts awkwardness.
Rigidity means being stiff or inflexible, opposite to deftness; the player's ability to move through gaps shows flexibility, not rigidity.

sentenceSets.sentence: The author's deftness at character development made even minor figures memorable and emotionally resonant.

Talent means natural ability or gift, close to deftness but describing innate ability rather than demonstrated facility and technique.
Finesse means skillful and delicate handling, very close to deftness, but finesse emphasizes elegance and subtlety rather than overall creative facility.
Artistry means creative skill and technique, close to deftness but emphasizing creative vision rather than the facility in execution.

Proficiency means a high degree of skill, related to deftness but emphasizing overall competence rather than smooth facility.
Acuity means sharpness of perception or understanding, related to character development but not describing the facility in creating memorable figures.
